title: Escape Rooms for Families and Teens: Tips and Ideas
description: Escape rooms for families and teenagers: how they work, minimum ages, picking the right room, plus treasure trails and geocaching for puzzle lovers on a budget.
intro: Sixty minutes, a locked room and a ticking clock. Escape rooms are one of the best ways to get teens and parents working as a team. Here’s how to pick one.

image.alt: A neon sign for escape rooms

blocks.title: Scout’s escape room verdict
blocks.text: Ask for a beginner or family room, check the minimum age, and don’t be shy about asking for hints. Everyone does!

sections.html: Your team is locked in a themed room and has to find clues and solve puzzles to get out, usually within 60 minutes. A game host watches and gives hints if you get stuck. Most rooms have a minimum age, and younger players often need an adult in the team.

• Choose a beginner or family room for your first go.
  • Check if the theme is scary. Horror rooms often have higher age limits.
  • Look at group sizes: most rooms take 2 to 6 players.
  • Mobile escape games and puzzle boxes are a cheaper option at home.

Read Scout’s escape room tips for families.

faqs.q: What age can kids do escape rooms?
faqs.a: It varies by venue and room. Many family rooms welcome children from around 8 to 10 with an adult, while scarier rooms have higher limits. Check before booking.

faqs.q: Are escape rooms good for teenagers?
faqs.a: Yes. They’re one of the most popular teen activities and work brilliantly for birthdays.
